notes: The 1985 format is COPY text-name-1 [{OF|IN} library-name-1] [REPLACING {pseudo-text-1|identifier-1|literal-1|word-1} BY {pseudo-text-2|identifier-2|literal-2|word-2} ...]. ParseCopyStatement/ReadCopyName read it, GateCopyPhrase refuses the 2002 literal names and SUPPRESS at 85 (COBOL0900), OperandScreen.PartialWord refuses LEADING/TRAILING, and ParseReplacingOperands refuses a pair without BY (the witness, COBOL2449), an empty REPLACING and a second REPLACING. Probes at --std 85 (classes b, c, d): pseudo-text, word, literal, qualified identifier, subscripted identifier, OF and IN library, multi-pair all accepted and replaced correctly; COPY "CB1", OF "LIB1", SUPPRESS [PRINTING], REPLACING LEADING, REPLACING., X Y (no BY), X BY ., OF ., OF LIB1 OF LIB1, a second REPLACING and COPY. each refused. DEFECT: ReadOperand reads identifier-1/identifier-2 as a word with OF/IN qualifiers and at most ONE balanced parenthesized group, so a 1985 identifier with subscripts AND a reference-modifier (T (2) (1:1)) and a function-identifier (FUNCTION LENGTH (X), identifier format 1 under Amendment 1) are refused with COBOL2449 'BY and the replacement operand must follow'. §1985:IV.4.3.8.5.1: a data-name 'must be followed by a syntactically correct combination of qualifiers, subscripts, or reference modifiers'; §1985:XII.2.4 GR4: 'For purposes of matching, identifier-1, word-1, and literal-1 are treated as pseudo-text'. The pseudo-text spelling of the same operands (==T (2) (1:1)==, ==FUNCTION LENGTH (X)==) works, which locates the defect in ReadOperand alone. kb/Work PB5469 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read4/rd-01.json).

next.reason: 1985: "REPLACING {==pseudo-text-1== | identifier-1 | literal-1 | word-1} BY {==pseudo-text-2== | identifier-2 | literal-2 | word-2}"; 2023: "REPLACING {==pseudo-text-1== BY ==pseudo-text-2== | {LEADING|TRAILING} ==partial-word-1== BY ==partial-word-2==}". 2023 COPY REPLACING accepts only pseudo-text or partial-word operands; the identifier, literal and word operands are gone. It adds a literal text name, a literal library name and SUPPRESS PRINTING.
